responsibility: Implements the procedural half of the IQ2000 GCC backend: the target-hook code and helper routines that turn the macro and machine-description definitions into actual code-generation behavior. This file owns IQ2000-specific frame layout state and prologue/epilogue support, calling convention decisions for arguments, varargs, and return values, address legitimization and cost modeling, register/mode legality checks, builtin expansion, assembly-output helpers such as operand printing and trampoline generation, and delay-slot or branch-related bookkeeping used around RTL expansion and final emission. In short, it is the main C implementation file that supplies the target-specific algorithms and TARGET_* hook bodies consumed by the rest of the IQ2000 port.
same_name_distinction: This is the procedural implementation file for the IQ2000 port: it supplies the TARGET hook bodies and helper code that act on the machine model defined elsewhere, including frame computation state, address legitimization, cost handling, builtin expansion, operand printing, and trampoline/prologue support. Unlike iq2000.h it does not declare the compile-time target macros and ABI/register layout policy, unlike iq2000.md it does not define RTL insn patterns or delay-slot/scheduling descriptions, and unlike iq2000.opt it is not the option table for -march/-mcpu and target masks.
